objectives: Read a short controlled /n/ passage across multiple connected sentences.
Sequence explicit events using first, next and last relationships.
Recall details and support answers with information from the passage.
concepts: Connected-text comprehension requires holding information across sentences.
Sequence depends on tracking event order rather than isolated sentence meaning.
Text evidence should be located in the passage before answering.

definitions.definition: Putting events in the order in which they occur.
The central meaning or overall point of a short text.
Information explicitly stated in the text that supports an answer.

workedExamples: First: Nan sat at a mat. Next: Nan sat. Last: Nan had a map.
What did Nan have? → a map, stated in the final sentence.
If the order is uncertain, reread each sentence and mark first/next/last.
commonMistakes: Adding events not stated in the passage.
Confusing a detail with the main idea.
revisionPoints: Read → track events → sequence → locate evidence → answer.

conceptual: Identify first, next and last events.
application: Locate explicit details in connected text.
higherOrderThinking: Explain why rereading improves sequencing accuracy.
mixedReview: Decode, sequence, recall and answer text-based questions.

formulaOrFactBank: Sequencing = identify event + position in text
mistakeBasedRevision: If order is confused, reread one sentence at a time and label first/next/last.
If a detail is forgotten, locate its sentence.
weakTopicRevision: Read the passage twice and retell all three events in order.

activities.name: Event ordering
steps: Place first, next and last in order.

outcomes: Learner reads the controlled passage with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner sequences three explicit events with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner recalls explicit details with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner answers using information stated in the passage rather than guessing.

questions.question: Read: “Nan sat at a mat. Nan sat. Nan had a map.” Who is the passage about?
Which event happened after Nan sat at a mat?
Which order is correct?
options: sat at a mat → sat → had a map
had a map → sat → sat at a mat

questions.question: Why should the reader reread the passage?
options: To confirm the order and details

questions.question: If the reader forgets what Nan had, what should they do?
options: Reread the sentence about what Nan had

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Nan sits at a mat and has a map

questions.question: Which question checks sequence?
options: How many letters are in Nan?

questions.question: What should a text-based answer come from?
What is the main goal of this lesson?
options: Read a controlled /n/ passage, sequence events and answer from text evidence
